style: Offset basalt trikuta with a later timber Garuda Mandapa and limewashed masonry shikharas
key_structures: Western Mahadwar, with Nagarkhana above the gate
Red-tiled Garuda Mandapa with square timber columns and foliated arches
Mukha or Ganesha Mandapa, Kasav Chowk, Pitali Umbartha, Sabha Mandapa and Antarala
West-facing Ambabai, south-facing Mahakali and north-facing Mahasaraswati sanctums
Upper Matulinga shrine, approached through the Nandi Mandapa
Three outdoor bhadra niches with Balaji, Katyayani and Gauri Shankar
Kashi Vishweshwar with Kashi Kund and the Navagraha ceiling-panel mandapa
special_features: During Kiranotsav, sunset rays reach the image through the western entrance and aligned halls
Ambabai is represented by a standing four-armed black-stone icon carrying citron, mace, shield and bowl
The northern courtyard mandapa has nine ceiling panels, described in the Gazetteer in connection with the directional guardians
period: Medieval stone core with later rebuilding and a nineteenth-century western hall
renovation_history: The archaeological survey distinguishes the layered work on the three sanctums and the later Garuda Mandapa. The current lighter shikharas reflect later rebuilding.
